review.summary: Scope reviewed: only the supplied migration SQL and the reported test receipt. I did not look at the test harness, UI, deployed roles or a populated database. Both earlier MINOR findings look fixed in the SQL. (1) Writes to sessions that are bound to an intake are now rechecked on every insert and update. Changing anchorAt or admissionSessionId on a bound session is rejected, and the session's scope (vendor, live, version, admission), anchorAt >= issuedAt and expiresAt <= the intake's expiry are checked against the intake row. A NULL anchorAt or expiresAt fails closed. Normal progress or close updates that don't extend expiresAt still pass after the intake expires. (2) The unexpected-grant check now includes column grants (attacl), and an attacl of NULL produces no rows, which is correct. If default privileges grant to any role other than PUBLIC, anon, authenticated or service_role, the migration fails closed. Parent cascade looks right: the intake delete guard only allows deletion once the version row is gone, and the session foreign key is NO ACTION, checked at the end of the statement. Inside the migration, BEGIN/COMMIT with SET LOCAL timeouts gives all-or-nothing rollback. One conditional MINOR remains. The session guard doesn't fix its timezone, so if LiveMetricSession stores timestamps without a timezone, the new time-bound check depends on the connection's timezone. Untested interaction: closing a session late (after the intake expires) when the close also rewrites expiresAt would now be rejected. The receipt only shows a close within the intake lifetime. All stated known limitations still apply unchanged: legacy NULL intake, no positive coverage producer, NULL or pre-start epochs uncertifiable, no populated upgrade, load or deployed-role proof, trust in table and function owners and superusers, TTL renewal, Next signed HTTP auth and live/WHEP unverified, and the synchronized20 Serializable gate at 7 successes and 13 failures (NOT_READY). The test receipt and this review do not certify a release.

findings.area: wp20_metric_session_intake_guard: function header SET clauses and the NEW.anchorAt/NEW.expiresAt vs i.issuedAt/i.expiresAt comparison
findings.issue: The session guard doesn't fix its timezone. If LiveMetricSession.anchorAt/expiresAt are timestamp without time zone (Prisma's default DateTime mapping), comparing them with the intake's TIMESTAMPTZ columns converts them using whatever TimeZone the connection has set.
findings.evidence: wp20_metric_playback_intake_guard sets timezone='UTC' and uses AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' for LiveViewerSession.expiresAt. This shows the schema mixes timestamp types. wp20_metric_session_intake_guard only sets search_path and row_security, then compares NEW columns directly with i.issuedAt and i.expiresAt (TIMESTAMPTZ(3)).
findings.impact: If a connection uses a UTC+N timezone, a bound session can get expiresAt up to N hours past the intake's expiry, or anchorAt before issuedAt. That partly undoes fix 1. A UTC-N connection would wrongly reject valid writes. This only applies if the session columns have no timezone and a connection isn't on UTC.
findings.recommended_fix: Add SET timezone='UTC' to wp20_metric_session_intake_guard. If the columns are timestamp without time zone, also compare (NEW."anchorAt" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') and (NEW."expiresAt" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'), matching the intake guard.
findings.required_test: Bind a session, then with SET TIME ZONE 'Asia/Tokyo' (and separately 'America/Los_Angeles') try an UPDATE that pushes expiresAt just past the intake's expiry and one that sets expiresAt exactly equal to it. Expect a 23514 rejection and a success respectively, whatever the session timezone. Also check the LiveMetricSession column types in the catalog.
